newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar firm, may hit a high in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar firm, may hit a high in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is expected to be firm against the yen during Asian trading time on Thursday after rising overnight due to data showing robust U.S. economic growth. Dealers said it may rise above 127.16 yen, its highest level since August 1992.
On the topside, option-linked sales to avoid hitting knock-out points around 127.30 yen and lingering concerns about possible dollar-selling intervention are expected to weigh on dollar.
But dealers added that the greenback could jump if it clearly breaks through 127.30 yen.

"Option-linked sales and wariness over possible intervention may encourage traders to take profits on the topside, but steady bids will emerge on any dips," a city bank dealer said, adding that the dollar will be supported near 126.80-90 yen.

The dollar rallied to session highs after the Commerce Department reported the economy grew 5.6 percent during the first three months of this year -- its fastest clip in more than nine years. It also prompted celebration in U.S. stock and bond markets with the Dow Jones industrials index rising above the 7,000 level irst time since March 13.

"The strong U.S. data, coupled with strong U.S. stocks, was bullish for the dollar," a trust bank dealer said, adding the speed of the dollar's rise may accelerate once it clearly breaks through 127.30 yen. He added that if Japanese investors decide to actively buy dollars, that would also give the greenback a chance to rise further.
But he said: "Those investors could also wait till next week after the release of U.S. jobs data on Friday... They usually start buying aggressively in May and June."
The city bank dealer said the dollar is likely to be supported just below 1.73 marks during Asian trading time.
